name: zeroclaw
notes: zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw, Rust, Apache-2.0 / MIT dual, actively pushed. Runs as a daemon (`zeroclaw daemon`) with an HTTP and WebSocket gateway, and keeps memory in SQLite. Rust plus a daemon plus SQLite makes it the second-closest architectural comparison to Brain after OpenFang.

Pinned to release v0.8.4, the latest at 2026-08-28. Installed from the project's own GitHub release asset zeroclaw-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz, checked against the SHA256SUMS published beside it — not built from source, so the binary measured is the one the project ships.

It is single-instance and single-user by design: one configured agent per installation, one TOML config, and multi-channel means one agent reachable from many places rather than many concurrent sessions. So throughput at N concurrent sessions and a per-session memory ramp are NOT declared here. Running them would measure something the project never claimed to do, and publishing the result would be a straw man.
The background memory sampler still records its footprint over time on every probe, which is the memory question that is fair to ask of a single-operator daemon.

Driven over `GET /ws/chat`, which is what its own dashboard uses. The HTTP surface cannot answer these probes: `POST /api/sessions/{id}/messages` only appends to the session log and never reaches the agent, and `POST /webhook` does run a turn but is rate limited per client key, emits no stream to time a first byte against, and has no session-create call.
Config differences from a stock install are listed at the top of launch.sh: pairing off on loopback, the scripted provider, and one named agent because zeroclaw has no default agent.

Its round_trip distribution is almost flat and does not match its ttfb: over 200 turns in one session, ttfb had a p50 of 9.6 ms while round_trip sat at p50 50.99 / p90 51.01 / min 49.99 ms — a spread of one millisecond across the middle 90%, and unchanged as the transcript grew. A turn's completion is therefore paced by something fixed of about 40 ms after the first assistant chunk rather than by the work in the turn. The cause was not traced to a line of zeroclaw's source, so it is recorded as an observation and not as a claim about their design; anyone quoting the round_trip figure should quote the ttfb beside it.

The scripted provider is hit TWICE per turn, not once. The second call is zeroclaw's memory consolidation, which its own source calls fire-and-forget: with the default SQLite memory backend and auto-save on, every completed turn spawns a background extraction call. It is off the turn's critical path — it starts after the reply is persisted and the `done` frame is sent — so it is not inside the latency numbers, but it is real work the daemon does per turn at its defaults, and it is why the runner's fixture-call count is 2x the turns driven rather than the 1x that would signal a cache.

cold_start.definition: process launch on a fresh data directory until the first turn is served; one-time installation untimed

recovery.definition: kill -9 after 50 turns, relaunch on the same data, until the same session serves a turn whose model request carries its history

create.definition: chat WebSocket upgrade until the gateway has answered the client's connect frame — zeroclaw's session create, after which the session accepts a message

ttfb.definition: message frame submitted until the first assistant `chunk` frame on the same socket; pointed at the scripted provider through a `providers.models.custom` entry

round_trip.definition: message frame submitted until the `done` frame carrying the completed reply
